clue.text: Unfriendly presenter edges away from Miles

indicators.note: when the edges go away, only the inside of the word stays, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: a host presents a television show
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A grumpy television presenter keeps his distance from someone called Miles.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles reads as a person's name, but it is just a word to be trimmed, losing its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and unfriendly are plain synonyms describing someone showing antagonism toward others.

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drunk has been celebrating loudly, yet it ends in misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a noun for the person cheering, but it signals the rearrangement. Hard cheese is a British informal expression of mock sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is chiefly British slang for tough luck, often said with little real sympathy.

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a seer is a prophet with visions

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a prophet off toward Ankara, Turkey's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's capital' wants to be Ankara; here capital means only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or direct something along a chosen course, a straightforward verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: generally, for the most part
second meaning: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' suggests being confused; the question mark flags the literal reading, since the main is the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for generally or on the whole, and read literally means located on the open ocean.

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle within a game turns out to be tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so the fodder 'in game' is complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something puzzling and hard to understand, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: audibly means in a way that can be heard, so the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: letting out a long breath to show you are let down

explanation.surface: A sports team groans aloud after a disappointing result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in a sporting contest, as in picking sides for a match.

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very northern' reads as describing the child, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child of his parents, so the general word covers him.

clue.text: Notwithstanding these tips, editor's upset to some extent

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
only partly, so just a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Despite some helpful pointers, an editor is somewhat annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'these tips, editor' and read upward; the comma is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are prepositions meaning in spite of something, plain synonyms used in formal writing.

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who complains from time to time and is sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' could be the bird or a complaint; here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to feel sorrow or remorse over it, a literary synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Narrowest hotel bar established on seafront at last

indicators.note: at last points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an inn is a pub, a place with a bar
EST is the standard abbreviation for established

explanation.surface: The skinniest hotel bar on the promenade has finally been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the seafront letter first, before the rest in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest and thinnest are both superlatives describing the least width, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Doctor envies mate from Hanoi, perhaps

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A physician is jealous of a friend who comes from Hanoi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is a verb signalling the rearrangement; 'perhaps' shows Hanoi is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam, so someone from that city is an example of a person of that nationality.

clue.text: Cut scarves shorter at both ends

indicators.note: trimming at both ends leaves only the interior letters of the word

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone trims a pile of scarves to make them shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' could be an adjective for the scarves, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut something, such as meat or wood, with a blade, a direct verb synonym.

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gulp down a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail made from gin or vodka with vermouth, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are smashed up and reassembled

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sold gin, then got wrecked on it afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' suggests being drunk, fitting the gin, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailing is the business of offering goods to the public, so it is a kind of commercial sales activity.

clue.text: Catch significant other briefly coming back

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a partner is someone's spouse or lover

explanation.surface: Someone meets their spouse for a short while on their return home.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten the word for a significant other, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch someone in a trap or by trickery, a close verb synonym.

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A dispute over rent payments leads to an angry row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it means ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, a specific example of the general weather word.

clue.text: Large plant in extremely short road

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a tree is a large woody plant

explanation.surface: A big tree grows on a very short stretch of road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely short' reads as very brief, but it means the outer letters of 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, lined with buildings, a near synonym.

clue.text: Entertain king for example with beer

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Hosting a monarch, for instance, by serving him a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it introduces the king as an instance, but it supplies its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to amuse or treat guests lavishly, often with stories or food and drink.

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
to call someone on the phone is to ring them

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A saint named George who turned out to be from abroad, like England's patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' suggests 'named', but it means telephoned, in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange in an older sense means foreign or alien, from somewhere unfamiliar, as in strange lands.

parts.note: to be home is to be in

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: aid is charitable help

explanation.surface: A rural estate gives its charity donation back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country home' reads as one phrase, a house in the countryside, but 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, a specific example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Greek character with key star's inside

parts.note: DEL is the delete key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its middle, with the outer letters stripped away

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Greek figure carries the key to a celebrity's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key or musical key, but it is a computer key.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is an example of such a letter.

clue.text: Tense friend in France eating the first bit of red meat

indicators.note: something eating takes food inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense
ami is French for friend

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An anxious French friend nibbles at some red meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is a grammatical tense; the two joined pieces enclose the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned smoked beef, often served in sandwiches, so it is an example of cured meat.

indicators.note: saying something will avoid a place means it stays out of it, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to skip the taxi to dodge the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' reads as the speaker, but the letter I is what will leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax is a levy imposed by government, so it is a kind of charge or fee.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: life is existence
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A life lacking any good fiction to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine fiction' looks like a pair, quality literature, but 'fine' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is an untrue statement, so it is a made-up fiction or falsehood.

clue.text: Try to persuade company beginning to adopt social network

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word
X is the social media platform formerly called Twitter

explanation.surface: Urging a business to start using a social media site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try to persuade company' reads as one action, but 'company' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to gently urge someone into doing something by flattery or patience.

parts.note: ENG is the abbreviation for English
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: An English political party makes a strong impression on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party after 'English', but it is a dance event.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is literally to cut marks into a surface, and figuratively to fix something firmly in memory.
